title: Why Planes Can’t Fly Higher Than 40,000 Feet
fullText: You are sitting in an airplane, cruising along comfortably, looking out at a brilliant blue sky above you. And here's something that might have crossed your mind. If planes can fly this high, why don't they just go higher? More altitude means thinner air. Thinner air means less drag. Less drag means the engines don't have to work as hard. So why does every commercial flight seem to top out somewhere between 35,000 and 40,000 ft? What exactly is stopping them? The answer isn't what most people expect. The atmosphere itself starts fighting back. Let's start with why altitude is attractive in the first place. When a plane climbs higher, the air around it gets thinner, and thinner [snorts] air creates less resistance against the aircraft. That means the engines can push the plane forward more efficiently. Fuel burns slower. The plane travels further on less. From a pure efficiency standpoint, the higher you go, the better. Airlines love efficiency because efficiency means lower operating costs and lower ticket prices. So the temptation to fly as high as possible is completely logical. But here is where it gets interesting. The same thin air that reduces drag also starts causing serious problems. A jet engine works by pulling in air, compressing it, mixing it with fuel, igniting it, and pushing the exhaust out the back. It needs air to do this. Specifically, it needs oxygen. And the higher you climb, the less oxygen there is available. At 40,000 ft, the air is already extremely thin. Push much higher and the engine simply cannot pull in enough oxygen to combust fuel properly. They start losing power, not suddenly, gradually, but enough to matter enormously. At the same time, the wings are facing their own crisis. Wings generate lift by using air flow. As the plane moves forward, air flows over and under the wing in a way that creates pressure differences. That pressure difference is what holds the aircraft up. But if the air becomes too thin, there isn't enough of it flowing over the wings to generate the lift needed to stay airborne. The plane would have to fly faster and faster just to maintain the same amount of lift. And this is where something remarkable happens. At very high altitude, the window between flying safely and disaster becomes incredibly narrow. On one side, you have a speed that is too slow. The wings stop generating enough lift and the plane stalls. It loses control and begins to fall. On the other side, you have a speed that is too fast. The plane approaches the speed of sound and starts experiencing severe structural stress that it simply wasn't designed to handle. At cruise altitude, these two limits are already fairly close together, but push the aircraft even higher. and those two limits begin to squeeze inward toward each other like a closing gap. Pilots call this the coffin corner. It sounds dramatic because it is. At that point, flying the aircraft within a safe speed range becomes almost impossible to maintain. Too slow and you stall. Too fast and the airframe starts to break down. The margin for error shrinks to almost nothing. This is the invisible ceiling that commercial aviation has built its entire operation around. It isn't a wall. It's a zone where everything stops working well at the same time. There's more to it as well. The cabin you're sitting in is pressurized. The aircraft pumps air in continuously to keep the pressure inside at a comfortable level, roughly equivalent to sitting at 6,000 to 8,000 ft above sea level. This system works well up to a point, but the higher the plane climbs, the harder the pressurization system has to work and the greater the pressure difference between the inside and outside of the fuselage. That difference puts stress on the entire structure of the aircraft. The windows, the walls, the seals, everything is being pulled outward by that pressure. Aircraft are designed to handle this, but there are structural limits. push too high and the forces involved become dangerous. So what you end up with is not one limit but several limits arriving at the same time. The engines need air, the wings need air, the cabin needs to stay pressurized without tearing the plane apart. And the speed window narrows dangerously the higher you go. The altitude where commercial planes cruise between 35,000 and 40,000 ft is not an arbitrary number. It is the sweet spot where all of these systems work together most efficiently. The air is thin enough to reduce drag and burn less fuel, but thick enough for the engines to breathe. Thick enough for the wings to generate lift at a reasonable speed, and manageable enough for the pressurization system to keep everyone comfortable inside. That's the thing about commercial aviation that often goes unnoticed. The aircraft doesn't dominate the sky. It finds the precise layer of the atmosphere where it can work in harmony with the conditions around it. Every flight you've ever taken has been a carefully balanced negotiation between gravity, air pressure, engine performance, and structural limits. The sky is vast, but the usable part of it is surprisingly thin. Next time you look out that window and see nothing but blue above you, you'll know exactly why the plane is sitting right where it is. Not because it can't go higher, but because where it is happens to be exactly right. If you enjoyed this video, please like and subscribe to Simple Concepts Explained.

segments.viText: Quá nhanh và khung máy bay bắt đầu bị hỏng.

segments.text: The margin for error shrinks to almost nothing.
segments.viText: Biên độ sai sót giảm xuống gần như không có gì.

segments.text: This is the invisible ceiling that commercial aviation has built its entire operation around.
segments.viText: Đây là trần vô hình mà hàng không thương mại đã xây dựng xung quanh nó trong toàn bộ hoạt động của mình.

segments.text: It isn't a wall.
segments.viText: Nó không phải là một bức tường.

segments.text: It's a zone where everything stops working well at the same time.
segments.viText: Đó là khu vực mà mọi thứ ngừng hoạt động tốt cùng một lúc.

segments.text: There's more to it as well.
segments.viText: Có nhiều hơn thế nữa.

segments.text: The cabin you're sitting in is pressurized.
segments.viText: Cabin bạn đang ngồi có áp suất.

segments.text: The aircraft pumps air in continuously to keep the pressure inside at a comfortable
segments.viText: Máy bay bơm không khí vào liên tục để giữ áp suất bên trong ở mức thoải mái

segments.text: level, roughly equivalent to sitting at 6,000 to 8,000 ft above sea level.
segments.viText: ngang bằng, gần tương đương với việc ngồi ở độ cao 6.000 đến 8.000 ft so với mực nước biển.

segments.text: This system works well up to a point, but the higher the plane climbs,
segments.viText: Hệ thống này hoạt động tốt ở một mức độ nào đó, nhưng máy bay càng lên cao,

segments.text: the harder the pressurization system has to work and the greater the pressure difference
segments.viText: hệ thống điều áp phải làm việc càng vất vả và chênh lệch áp suất càng lớn

segments.text: between the inside and outside of the fuselage.
segments.viText: giữa bên trong và bên ngoài thân máy bay.

segments.text: That difference puts stress on the entire structure of the aircraft.
segments.viText: Sự khác biệt đó gây áp lực lên toàn bộ kết cấu của máy bay.

segments.text: The windows, the walls, the seals, everything is being pulled outward by that pressure.
segments.viText: Những cửa sổ, những bức tường, những tấm bịt ​​kín, mọi thứ đều bị sức ép đó kéo ra ngoài.

segments.text: Aircraft are designed to handle this, but there are structural limits.
segments.viText: Máy bay được thiết kế để xử lý việc này, nhưng có những giới hạn về cấu trúc.

segments.text: push too high and the forces involved become dangerous.
segments.viText: đẩy quá cao và các lực liên quan trở nên nguy hiểm.

segments.text: So what you end up with is not one limit but several limits arriving
segments.viText: Vì vậy, những gì bạn đạt được không phải là một giới hạn mà là một số giới hạn

segments.text: at the same time.
segments.viText: cùng một lúc.

segments.text: The engines need air, the wings need air, the cabin needs to stay pressurized
segments.viText: Động cơ cần không khí, cánh cần không khí, cabin cần duy trì áp suất

segments.text: without tearing the plane apart.
segments.viText: mà không xé nát chiếc máy bay.

segments.text: And the speed window narrows dangerously the higher you go.
segments.viText: Và cửa sổ tốc độ càng thu hẹp một cách nguy hiểm khi bạn càng lên cao.

segments.text: The altitude where commercial planes cruise between 35,000 and 40,000 ft is not an
segments.viText: Độ cao mà máy bay thương mại bay trong khoảng từ 35.000 đến 40.000 ft không phải là

segments.text: arbitrary number.
segments.viText: số tùy ý.

segments.text: It is the sweet spot where all of these systems work together most efficiently.
segments.viText: Đó là điểm tuyệt vời nơi tất cả các hệ thống này hoạt động cùng nhau hiệu quả nhất.

segments.text: The air is thin enough to reduce drag and burn less fuel, but thick
segments.viText: Không khí đủ mỏng để giảm lực cản và đốt cháy ít nhiên liệu hơn, nhưng dày

segments.text: enough for the engines to breathe.
segments.viText: đủ để động cơ thở.

segments.text: Thick enough for the wings to generate lift at a reasonable speed, and manageable
segments.viText: Đủ dày để cánh tạo ra lực nâng ở tốc độ hợp lý và có thể điều khiển được

segments.text: enough for the pressurization system to keep everyone comfortable inside.
segments.viText: đủ để hệ thống điều áp giúp mọi người thoải mái bên trong.

segments.text: That's the thing about commercial aviation that often goes unnoticed.
segments.viText: Đó là điều mà hàng không thương mại thường không được chú ý.

segments.text: The aircraft doesn't dominate the sky.
segments.viText: Máy bay không thống trị bầu trời.

segments.text: It finds the precise layer of the atmosphere where it can work in harmony
segments.viText: Nó tìm thấy lớp khí quyển chính xác nơi nó có thể hoạt động hài hòa

segments.text: with the conditions around it.
segments.viText: với các điều kiện xung quanh nó.

segments.text: Every flight you've ever taken has been a carefully balanced negotiation between gravity, air
segments.viText: Mỗi chuyến bay bạn từng thực hiện đều là một cuộc đàm phán được cân bằng cẩn thận giữa trọng lực, không khí

segments.text: pressure, engine performance, and structural limits.
segments.viText: áp suất, hiệu suất động cơ và giới hạn kết cấu.

segments.text: The sky is vast, but the usable part of it is surprisingly thin.
segments.viText: Bầu trời rộng lớn nhưng phần có thể sử dụng được của nó lại mỏng đến mức đáng kinh ngạc.

segments.text: Next time you look out that window and see nothing but blue above you,
segments.viText: Lần tới khi bạn nhìn ra ngoài cửa sổ đó và không thấy gì ngoài màu xanh phía trên bạn,

segments.text: you'll know exactly why the plane is sitting right where it is.
segments.viText: bạn sẽ biết chính xác tại sao máy bay lại ở đúng vị trí của nó.

segments.text: Not because it can't go higher, but because where it is happens to be
segments.viText: Không phải vì nó không thể cao hơn, mà vì nơi nó xảy ra là

segments.viText: chính xác đúng.
